tldr: Headlines across all nine buckets compress Greece's multi-day wildfire crisis into two dominant signals: fatal casualties (especially the midair helicopter collision near Athens on August 3 that killed two crew) and a response stretched past four consecutive days against wind-driven fires that won't yield. Canada, India, and China extend the frame outward to a pan-European or global wildfire emergency; all other outlets stay tightly on the Greek domestic front.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline to embed a direct quote from the crisis — '"The situation is out of control"' — surfacing the desperation of front-line responders at the homepage level, a register absent from all other outlet titles.

The only headline to link Greece's fires to US wildfires in the same title ('wildfires sweep Europe, US'), positioning the event as a global rather than exclusively European emergency — a framing divergence from all other outlets.

The only headline to use emotional mood language ('turns somber') rather than a factual statement of deaths, foregrounding collective grief over the operational fact of the crash — a tone absent from every other title.

The only headline to frame the wildfire crisis as a climate-weather story ('hot, dry summer maintains its grip on Europe'), connecting the disaster to a broader seasonal pattern not named in any other outlet's title.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, Greece's wildfire emergency is a story of death and exhaustion: firefighters dying while fighting fires entering their fourth consecutive day, with the midair helicopter collision near Athens serving as the universal news hook across all nine buckets.
